one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event falls in the 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08 window: Q3 2026 results. The date has not been announced yet, but Generac reported Q3 2025 on 2025-10-29 (EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02), so a late-October or early-November print is near-certain to land inside the window. Setup: management guided Q3 net sales growth in the 'high teens' with Q3 EBITDA margin similar to Q2 excluding tariff refunds, i.e. roughly $1.31-1.33B on the $1.114B Q3 2025 base; the consensus is $1.327B revenue and $2.43 EPS, after 14 downward EPS revisions in the prior 30 days, so the bar has been lowered. Residential is the risk: the 2026 residential guide assumes baseline outage activity for H2, while Q2 outages were more than 30% below baseline and NOAA forecast a below-normal Atlantic season with El Nino. I have not verified actual Q3 outage data, so this is a modest negative skew, not a call. C&I is the likely upside. The 8-K disclosed Amazon deliveries of about $2.4B across 2027-28, so the reported data center backlog should step up sharply from the $1.6B disclosed in July. Management may also give early 2027 colour, as it did with its 'may crush [the C&I doubling target] by next year' comment. Most of that news is already known and priced after the September jump. Generac's earnings-week moves have been large in both directions: -12.5% (Oct 2025), +22% (Feb 2026), +17% (Apr 2026) and -2.4% (Jul 2026). The stock is also up about 20% in the past month, from $187 to $225. I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred on $224.94 with a tiny positive drift and a one-month sigma of about 16.5%, a touch above the 56%/3.5 = 16% rule because of the earnings event. P(>= today's price) is about 0.51.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (60%) and EV/EBITDA (40%) applied to estimated NTM figures as of Oct-2027: NTM EPS $14.55 x 18x = $261.9; NTM adj. EBITDA $1.443B x 12x = EV $17.32B less ~$0.8B net debt over 60.3M diluted shares = $274.0. Blended ~$267.

inputs_detail.derivation: Average of Alpha Vantage FY2027 mean $12.668 (19 analysts) and StockAnalysis FY2027 $12.97: (12.668+12.97)/2 = 12.82.

FY27 consensus x 1.18. The +18% growth (vs +34% consensus FY27 growth) assumes data center volume keeps ramping as Amazon's ~$2.4B of 2027-28 deliveries (8-K) and the path to triple large-megawatt capacity within 12 months of July 2026 (Q2 call) carry into 2028. It is haircut for hyperscale margins that management says are lower than for non-hyperscale customers and for a residential base still recovering from below-baseline outages.
0.25 x 12.82 + 0.75 x 15.13 = 14.55 (roughly one quarter of FY27 and three quarters of FY28 remain in the forward year).

Peer median forward P/E 26.87x (range 14.1-30.8x). 18x sits inside the range, between the residential durable-goods peers (LII/AOS/RRX ~14x) and the data center electrical names (CAT/ETN/NVT/VRT/POWL 28-31x), and weights GNRC's ~45/55 Residential/C&I mix. It is below the median because GNRC earnings are outage-cyclical (adj. EPS fell from $7.27 in 2024 to $6.34 in 2025) and C&I segment EBITDA margin is only 14.6%. It is also slightly above today's ~17.5x on FY27 consensus and below the 21.7x current NTM P/E, allowing for some de-rating as growth normalises.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM adj. EBITDA $1.443B x 12x = EV $17.32B; net debt ~$0.8B; 60.3M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Average of Alpha Vantage $6.397B and StockAnalysis $6.50B.

2026 guidance is 20-21% including ~1.5 pts of one-off tariff refunds, i.e. 18.5-19.5% underlying (Q2 release/call). Add ~1 pt of operating leverage on +30% revenue (CFO: operating leverage drives margin expansion), partly offset by lower-margin hyperscale mix (CEO). 2025 margin was 17.0%.
FY27 x 1.13: continued data center ramp (Amazon 2027-28 deliveries, capacity tripling) on a larger base, with residential at roughly mid-single-digit growth.
+0.5 pt further operating leverage over FY27 estimate.

Peer median TTM EV/EBITDA 23.88x (range 10.4-35.0x); GNRC trades at 22.7x TTM. 12x forward is consistent with the 18x P/E (12x on $1.44B gives ~$274/share or ~18.8x NTM EPS) and sits inside the peer range near the residential/industrial cluster (AOS 10.4x, LII 12.2x, RRX 12.6x), reflecting cyclicality.

Total debt ~$1.33B (10-Q: $1,281.0M long-term incl. finance leases + $48.3M short-term) less $264.9M cash = ~$1.06B at 6/30/26; StockAnalysis shows ~$1.14B. Less ~$0.35B of free cash flow over the next 12 months (2026 FCF guided ~$350M), no buybacks assumed (none in H1 2026).

59.006M outstanding at 7/31/26 + ~0.8M dilutive awards (Q2 diluted 59.64M vs basic 58.82M) + ~0.3-0.5M net treasury-method shares from the Amazon warrant (1,693,745 shares at $200.93; 307,954 vested immediately, the rest vesting with payments up to $8B).

bear.story: Data center deliveries slip or get resized as hyperscale capex pauses; the 10-Q flags cancellation rights and delivery requirements in DC contracts. C&I margins stay around 14-15% while capacity spending runs near 4.5-5% of sales. Residential stays weak if outages remain below baseline in an El Nino year and solar/storage is soft. FY28 EPS ~$11 x 14x (low end of peers, like LII/AOS/RRX) gives ~$150, near the pre-Amazon-deal lows of $175-185 less a de-rating.

base.story: The $1.35B of 2027-scheduled backlog plus Amazon's ~$2.4B of 2027-28 deliveries ship roughly on time as Sussex and Belvidere ramp. Revenue reaches ~$6.4-6.5B in 2027 (consensus), adj. EBITDA margin ~20% underlying, and the market pays ~18x NTM EPS of ~$14.55.

bull.story: The Amazon relationship trends toward its $8B payment ceiling, another hyperscaler converts, and capacity triples on schedule. C&I passes the Investor Day 'double in three years' goal in 2027, as the CEO suggested it might; a normal or active 2027 hurricane season revives home standby. FY28 EPS ~$17 x ~22x (still inside the peer range) gives ~$370.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 14.1x (RRX) to 30.8x (VRT); EV/EBITDA (trailing; forward not available on free sources) 10.4x (AOS) to 35.0x (VRT). GNRC today: 21.7x forward P/E, 22.7x TTM EV/EBITDA, ~17.5x FY27 consensus EPS.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 18x NTM P/E (Oct-2027) and 12x NTM EV/EBITDA, both inside the peer range and below the medians (26.9x and 23.9x TTM).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount to the median rests on persistent, documented features rather than a call on relative performance. (1) Earnings are cyclical and weather-driven: adj. EPS fell from $7.27 (2024) to $6.34 (2025) and Q4 2025 residential sales fell 23% on a weak outage year. (2) C&I segment adj. EBITDA margin is only 14.6% (Q2 2026, including ~2 pts of tariff refund), below the high-teens and twenties margins implied for electrical data center peers, and management says hyperscale margins run below other customers with no above-market pricing. (3) The data center revenue is concentrated in a few hyperscale customers under contracts with cancellation rights (10-Q risk factors), and Amazon's warrant ties ~2.9% potential dilution to its purchases. On the other side, faster revenue growth than most peers (consensus FY27 +32%) keeps the multiple well above the 14x residential-durables cluster, so 18x sits in the lower-middle of the range rather than at the bottom.

thesis_break_reason: A close below ~$160 is below where GNRC traded before the Amazon agreement (~$175-187 in late Aug/early Sep 2026), ~20% below the warrant strike of $200.93 and ~29% below today. It would most likely mean the market no longer believes the 2027 data center deliveries ($1.35B scheduled backlog plus Amazon's ~$2.4B over 2027-28) will convert at acceptable margins, for example a hyperscale order deferral or cancellation, capacity ramp problems at Sussex or Belvidere, or C&I margins compressing below ~12%, rather than ordinary residential/outage noise.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results: data center backlog update including Amazon, Q4 ramp, residential/outage commentary, possible early 2027 colour
Tariff policy changes in H2 2026 that could offset further IEEPA refund recovery (CFO flagged potentially higher tariffs)
Q4/FY2026 results and first full-year 2027 guidance (FY2025 results were released 2026-02-11)
Belvidere, IL packaging/fabrication facility expected operational; start of 2027 hyperscale deliveries
Firm product terms or added backlog from other hyperscale customers (management: a third is 'very early')
Q1 2027 results: first quarter of large-scale hyperscale shipments; margin read-through
Progress on tripling large-megawatt production capacity within ~12 months of July 2026
2027 Atlantic hurricane season and summer grid stress (home standby demand driver)

key_uncertainties: Whether the Amazon agreement is the 'second hyperscaler' from the Q2 call and is fully incremental to the $1.6B backlog. The 8-K does not say; I assume it is largely incremental, which is a judgment.
Margins on hyperscale volumes: management says they are lower than for non-hyperscale customers with no price premium. C&I EBITDA margin was 14.6% in Q2 2026 including ~2 pts of tariff refunds.
Execution of a ~3x capacity ramp (Sussex, Belvidere, plus Brazil/Mexico/India) while capex runs at ~4.5% of sales, with 40-45 week lead times as the competitive edge.
Hyperscale capex cycle risk and contract cancellation rights flagged in the 10-Q.
Residential: outages >30% below baseline in Q2 2026, a below-normal NOAA hurricane forecast, and soft residential solar/storage. The home standby recovery is unproven.
One-off tariff refunds (~$71M in Q2, ~$0.90/share) inflate 2026 EPS and reverse in 2027 comparisons; tariff policy could also reverse.
Dilution from the Amazon warrant (up to 1.69M shares, ~2.9%) as Amazon's purchases accumulate.
reasoning: Lane: primary documents. I read the Q2 2026 release and 10-Q, the Q2 call transcript, the 16 September 2026 Amazon 8-K, the FY2025 and Q1 2026 releases, the recast 2025 segment exhibit, the March 2026 segment-reorganisation 8-K, the FY2025 10-K and recent Form 4s. Fundamentals: 2025 sales were $4.21B, adj. EBITDA 17.0% and adj. EPS $6.34. The 2026 guide is mid-to-high-teens growth (~$4.9B), C&I up in the low 30s, residential up high-single digits, adj. EBITDA margin 20-21% including ~1.5 pts of one-off IEEPA tariff refunds, and FCF about $350M. The data center backlog was ~$1.6B at Q2, $1.35B of it scheduled for 2027. The September 8-K then disclosed an Amazon warrant (1.69M shares at $200.93, vesting against up to $8B of generator purchases) and ~$2.4B of initial deliveries in 2027-28. Management also has a path to roughly triple large-megawatt capacity within 12 months of July 2026. That supports consensus 2027 revenue of ~$6.4-6.5B and EPS of ~$12.7-13.0 (+34%). Things the recaps skip: C&I segment EBITDA margin is only 14.6% even with tariff help, management concedes hyperscale margins are lower and pricing is not above market, the 10-Q flags DC contract cancellation rights, and there were no buybacks in H1 2026. Insider selling is small and routine: the CEO sells 5,000 shares a month and holds ~545k. Valuation: 18x NTM EPS of $14.55 gives $261.9, and 12x NTM EBITDA of $1.443B gives $274.0. The blended fair value of ~$267 is ~18% above $224.94. The multiples sit below the 12-peer medians (26.9x P/E, 23.9x EV/EBITDA) because of outage-driven cyclicality and lower C&I margins. Distribution: a three-scenario mixture with bear $150 (27%), base ~$267 (48%) and bull $370 (25%), widened toward the stock's 56% realized volatility (it ranged $135-296 in a year with ±15-20% earnings weeks). I shaded the centre down from fair value because sell-side upside has been unreliable and the stock already re-rated ~20% in a month. That gives a median near $250 and P(>= $225) ~0.6. Tails stay fat: P(<= $135) ~11% and P(>= $394) ~12%. Limits: the investor-day deck and IR site returned 403, so I used no investor-day 2028 targets. Forward EV/EBITDA for peers was not available free, so the comps EV/EBITDA field holds trailing values. Peer data came from StockAnalysis pages, two per peer. Because the brief requires 12 peers, those data pages push the in-lane share of sources below 60%; excluding the comps table, most sources are primary filings or transcripts. I did not look up option prices or implied volatility.
